title: The System of the World

description.main: The third and final volume of Neal Stephenson's Baroque Cycle, set in early eighteenth-century London.
description.extended:
The System of the World closes the Baroque Cycle, Neal Stephenson's historical fiction about the birth of modern science and finance.

The novel opens with Daniel Waterhouse returning to England from Boston to settle the quarrel between Isaac Newton and Gottfried Leibniz over who invented calculus. An assassination attempt with a time bomb follows him, and Jack Shaftoe, working as a coiner, plots a heist at the Tower of London. Eliza meanwhile supports Princess Caroline of Hanover as the succession to Queen Anne is contested. Newton's work at the Mint and the Trial of the Pyx run through the plot. The title alludes to the third volume of Newton's Principia. William Morrow published it in September 2004, and it won the Locus Award for Best Science Fiction Novel and the Prometheus Award in 2005. It was also shortlisted for the Arthur C. Clarke Award.

It follows The Confusion and ends a project that ran across three books. Stephenson later turned to fiction set on another planet in Anathem and in the present day in Reamde.

notes: First hardcover edition (William Morrow, 2004). The Baroque Cycle, volume three; preceded by The Confusion.
